_comment: Canonical field definitions for every content element in this extension.
All blocks declare prefixFields: false, so a field identifier becomes a
tt_content column SHARED by every element that uses it. That is the point:
250 elements built from this vocabulary add a few dozen columns, while 250
elements each inventing their own field names would add well over a
thousand. It also means an editor who switches an element's type keeps the
The rule that follows: a field identifier here has ONE meaning and ONE type
across the whole catalog. If a new element needs a subtly different flavour
of an existing field, it reuses the field and varies the label — it does not
Never name a field 'label': Content Blocks reserves it and the generated

header._note: The core header column. Every element that shows a title uses it, so the page module and search see a real title.

subheader._note: Core subheader column — the line under the title.

bodytext._note: Core rich text. For editorial prose.

eyebrow._note: The small label above a heading that says which section this is. Textarea with one row: the type is shared with Desiderio, whose columns these already are.

lead._note: One or two plain sentences introducing a band. Not rich text: a lead that carries formatting stops being a lead.

text._note: Plain body copy for elements whose text is short enough not to need the editor.

note._note: The small print under a band — a footnote, a caveat, a delivery condition.

caption._note: Media caption. Textarea with one row: the type is shared with Desiderio, whose columns these already are.

quote_text._note: The quotation itself, without quotation marks — the template draws those.

author._note: Person being quoted or credited. Textarea with one row: the type is shared with Desiderio, whose columns these already are.

role._note: Job title and company of the person in 'author'. Textarea with one row: the type is shared with Desiderio, whose columns these already are.

value._note: The number a metric shows, as text — '99.98%', '1.2M', '4.9'. Text rather than a number field because the unit and the formatting are part of the claim.

unit._note: What the value is measured in, when it is not part of the value itself.

price._note: Displayed price as text, because '€49', 'Free' and 'Let's talk' all belong in the same slot. Textarea with one row: the type is shared with Desiderio, whose column this already is.

period._note: Billing period shown after the price.

badge_text._note: Short marker on a card: 'Most popular', 'New', 'Beta'. Textarea with one row: the type is shared with Desiderio, whose columns these already are.

secondary_label._note: Text of the second, quieter action.

image._note: One image. Elements that show several use a collection instead.

icon._note: Semantic icon key, resolved by the shared icon registry at render time so switching icon library never rewrites a record.

variant._note: The element's own visual variants. Prefixed, because 'variant' means something different in every element.

tone._note: Which surface tone the band sits on. Shared vocabulary across the catalog.

align._note: Horizontal alignment of the band's text.

columns._note: How many columns a grid aims for. A hint, not a promise: the grid still reflows on the space it has.

featured._note: Marks this element as the emphasised one in a row of siblings.

reverse._note: Swaps the two halves of a split layout.
